chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Shihab, from Hisham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding a man who was in the course of an Obligatory Tawaaf (circumambulation), so the time for an Obligatory Salat (Prayer) caught him, he said: He should cut his Tawaaf and offer the Obligatory Prayer, then he should return and complete what remains of his Tawaaf.
ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if the time for obligatory prayer comes during the Tawaaf?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the principle of prioritizing the fixed-time Obligatory Prayer (Salat) over the continuous act of worship (Tawaaf), reflecting the Shia juristic view that the temporal constraint of prayer supersedes the ritual continuity of circumambulation. It underscores the balance between ritual completeness and the urgency of the five daily prayers, a key distinction in Shia fiqh compared to some Sunni schools that may allow completion of Tawaaf if the prayer time is short. The hadith serves as a practical legal precedent for pilgrims navigating the intersection of Hajj rituals and daily devotional duties.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Shihab, from Hisham, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding a man who was in an Obligatory Tawaaf, so he came across the Obligatory Salaat. Heasws said: ‘He should cut his Tawaaf, and he should offer the Obligatory Salaat (Prayer), then he should return and complete what remains upon him from his Tawaaf’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Shihab from Hisham who has said the following: “About a man who is in an obligatory Tawaf and obligatory Salat (prayer) commences, abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He can keep his Tawaf on hold, perform obligatory Salat (prayer), then return to his Tawaf where he had left to complete the remaining parts.’”
